subject: civil
audience: FE Civil candidates and civil engineering students
title: The Column That Buckled Near 497 kips
featured_title: THE COLUMN THAT BUCKLED NEAR 497 KIPS

presentation.challenge: The steel strength was not the first limit. Slender-column instability governed near 497 kips.

practice.primary_question: Why does Euler buckling load depend on effective length squared rather than only on material strength?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Checking compressive stress only and ignoring elastic instability in a slender column.

case_dna.target_misconception: A slender steel column's compressive capacity can be estimated from material strength alone without considering member length and end restraint.
case_dna.why_plausible: Axial stress P/A is familiar, and strength checks dominate many short-member calculations.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For a pinned-pinned column, Pcr=π²EI/L². With E=29,000 ksi, I=100 in^4, and L=240 in, Pcr≈497 kips.
case_dna.corrected_model: Slender-column stability depends strongly on effective length: Pcr=π²EI/(KL)². End conditions and length can govern before material compression strength.

problem_statement: A slender pinned-pinned steel column is 20 ft long with E=29,000 ksi and weak-axis I=100 in^4. A check focuses only on compressive stress and assumes the column can carry much more load. Estimate the Euler critical buckling load and determine how halving the effective length changes Pcr.
fixed_constraints: Elastic Euler model for this exercise

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The material had strength left. The column lost stability first.
gates.prompt: Which parameter makes slender-column stability strongly geometry-dependent?

options.label: Use Pcr=π²EI/(KL)² for elastic Euler buckling
options.reason: The model captures stiffness and effective-length effects.

options.label: Use only P=σA because buckling does not depend on length
options.reason: Slender columns can lose stability before a simple material-stress limit is reached.

options.label: Buckling load is inversely proportional to L, not L²
options.reason: Euler load varies with the inverse square of effective length.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the Euler load
gates.prompt: Approximately what critical load in kips results for K=1, L=240 in, E=29,000 ksi, I=100 in^4?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Increase axial load
gates.result: The ideal elastic critical load is about 497 kips.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the buckling load
gates.prompt: Use Pcr=π²(29,000)(100)/(240²). Enter Pcr in kips.
gates.hint: Use inches consistently with E in ksi and I in in^4.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The inverse-square length term controls slenderness sensitivity

cards.text: Pcr=π²EI/L²≈497 kips; halving effective length would multiply Pcr by four.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the column-capacity note
report: C3. Therefore length and end restraint do not matter until material compressive strength is reached.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: Slender-column instability depends strongly on effective length and flexural stiffness.

evidence_choices.label: Pcr=π²EI/(KL)² explicitly contains effective length squared
evidence_choices.reason: This directly shows why geometry and restraint matter.

correction.template: The ideal elastic Euler critical load is about {pcr} kips for the stated pinned-pinned column.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Increase Euler buckling resistance without changing E or I

options.label: Brace the column so the effective length is halved
options.reason: Because Pcr∝1/(KL)², halving effective length increases Euler load by a factor of four.

options.label: Double the unsupported length
options.reason: That reduces Pcr by a factor of four.

options.label: Keep the same effective length and ignore buckling
options.reason: The stability limit is a physical behavior, not a calculation option.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply effective-length scaling
gates.prompt: If a column's effective length is doubled while E and I stay constant, what happens to Euler Pcr?

options.label: It doubles
options.reason: Longer effective length reduces buckling capacity.

gates.explanation: Euler buckling load is inversely proportional to effective length squared.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the column-stability model
gates.confirmation: I confirm that slender-column capacity must consider buckling and effective length, not only axial material stress.

seo.seo_title: Euler Column Buckling: Why Effective Length Controls Pcr | FE E-046
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil Case E-046: a 20 ft pinned steel column with E=29,000 ksi and I=100 in^4 has Euler Pcr of about 497 kips.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Civil Euler buckling effective length
seo.excerpt: A slender column can lose stability before material strength is exhausted. Effective length enters Euler load as a squared term.
seo.direct_answer: For a pinned-pinned elastic column, Pcr=π²EI/L². With E=29,000 ksi, I=100 in^4, and L=240 in, Pcr≈497 kips. Because Pcr varies as 1/L², halving effective length increases the Euler load fourfold.

faqs.q: What is the Euler critical load formula?
What happens to Euler buckling load if effective length is halved?
faqs.a: It increases by a factor of four, all else equal.
